correctness.rationale: For n>2k classical EKR equality yields exactly n full-star complementary facets, all multiple intersections are simplices indexed by subsets of cardinality <=n-k, and the nerve has the claimed skeleton, wedge rank and (via equivariant Cech double complex) integral exterior-power module. For n=2k the graph is a matching, so the cut complex is the cross-polytope boundary. The transposition determinant of its anti-complement lattice is (-1)^(binom(2k-2,k-1)/2), which is negative precisely if k-1 has one binary 1. The direct verifier enumerates representative maximum independent families and all relevant intersection patterns, builds signed complement-pair actions for k=2..9 and verifies all conjugacy-class Lefschetz characters in six supercritical small cases. Finite checks corroborate, while the written EKR/nerve/chain/2-adic proof gives generality.

originality.rationale: Inspected original and latest papers on total-cut complexes, their duality, and their stable-Kneser-neighborhood motivation, as well as published-finding corpus near-matches for Kneser complexes, total-cut graph classes and symmetry. Known EKR equality, sphere skeleton and disconnected-graph boundary homotopy are acknowledged; the proposed contribution is the complete extremal Kneser transition plus integral S_n homology and the 2-adic orientation dichotomy. No equivalent theorem or dominating primary coverage was identified.
residual_risks: A non-indexed cut-complex classification may implicitly subsume one or both formulations; no universal uniqueness claim is made.
The n>2k homotopy type is a concise classical EKR-plus-nerve implication; originality is located in the combined two-regime integral symmetry classification, not solely the wedge count.
The disconnected matching boundary case is an instance of classical cross-polytope topology; only its S_{2k} determinant/arithmetic action is claimed as an extension.

value.rationale: The extremal cut level is intrinsic, set by the EKR maximum rather than arbitrary graph parameters. The result distinguishes the highly degenerate equality boundary n=2k, where there are exponentially many extremal families and one sphere, from n>2k, where exactly n stars give a much lower-dimensional sphere wedge. The actual integral S_n action is determined uniformly (exterior hook lattice), and a non-obvious arithmetic parity criterion distinguishes orientation-preserving from reversing symmetry exactly at the boundary. These determine symmetry/representation invariants that nonequivariant homology ranks cannot reveal; the result is a natural complete infinite-family classification, not a repeated small-table computation.
